paper.title: Algorithm 439: Product Type Three-point Gauss-Legendre Simpson Integration
paper.venue: Communications of the ACM 15(12), p. 1072 (Dec 1972), per the archive header. The frame item says 'TOMS 15,12'; the archive header says Communications of the ACM, so the frame label is taken as wrong and the header is used. The article itself is not read.
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/439.gz (article not fetched; ACM page not used)

code.commit: netlib CALGO archive 439.gz (shell archive; Fortran/Dp/Src/src.f, Fortran/Dp/Drivers/driver.f, Makefile, and the reference file Fortran/Dp/Drivers/res)
code.archive: downloaded by scout 2026-11-27 from netlib.org/toms/439.gz (HTTP 200, 2320 bytes). sha256 of 439.gz: sha256 81cfd10dead980d26565450b9f98bac46566f3d9da7b70552086feb4fd314407 (scout download, 2026-11-27).
code.note: Gunzip the archive and run it with /bin/sh in an empty directory, then build the driver from Fortran/Dp/Drivers with the archive's Makefile and compare its stdout with Fortran/Dp/Drivers/res.

claim.location: Shipped reference output Fortran/Dp/Drivers/res (inside 439.gz), block TEST01: integral of F(X)*G(X) from -1 to 1 with F=1, G=1/(1+x**2), table row N = 10, VINT = 2.65082 (the printed 'Exact' is 2.65164, not the claim).

reference.sha256: not computed for the member; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.paper_value: VINT 2.65082 at N = 10 as printed by the shipped driver (the paper is not read).
claim.metric: VINT for TEST01 at N = 10, as printed by the driver in the 5-decimal format of the res file, compared as an absolute number
claim.determinism: deterministic (fixed integrand, fixed N, no random numbers)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The printed value has 5 decimals, so its rounding step is 1e-5 and the claim tolerance of 1e-5 allows one rounding step of difference from the printed reference (equal to two half-steps). Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 2 minutes: one Fortran build of the driver and one run.
cost.data_licence: Netlib CALGO archive; licence per the archive's own notices (the rerun should record it).

why: The driver runs the product-type Gauss-Legendre Simpson rule for a fixed integrand and prints the N=10 value; no closed form gives that quadrature output at N=10, so the rerun must execute the Fortran method.
